prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single, reputable “beginner crypto education” site that also runs a live trading/experiment account and routinely publishes its losses in a full audited way. That combination creates legal, ethical and liability problems, so most good educators separate plain-English teaching from live trading performance.

What I recommend instead
- Coin Bureau — best plain-English, beginner-friendly walkthroughs (how tokens work, wallets, staking, risks). Clear explanations and tokenomics numbers, but it’s an educational channel, not a live P&L sheet.
- Glassnode Studio or Messari/Coin Metrics — if you want real, on‑chain and market numbers. These sites provide data and visualizations you can verify on-chain.
- DeFi Dad and The Defiant — if you want hands‑on tutorials and transparent experiments. DeFi Dad posts on‑chain transactions and step‑by‑step guides you can verify yourself (so “losses” from an experiment are public on Etherscan if they show addresses). The Defiant documents DeFi experiments and sometimes publishes post‑mortems.
- Bankless — beginner-friendly, practical guides (wallets, DeFi basics) plus a community that publishes case studies.

How to get the “publishes losses” behavior you want
- Follow creators who publish addresses/txns and do post‑mortems. If they post wallet addresses and full transactions, you can verify gains/losses yourself on-chain.
- Prefer content that includes actual screenshots of transactions, on‑chain links (Etherscan), and explicit post‑trade writeups.
- Look for independent post‑mortems and security incident writeups (they often disclose losses and cause).

If you tell me whether you want: basic investing/holding advice, DeFi how‑to’s, or on‑chain data analysis, I can give one tailored “best” single recommendation and a few specific creators whose experiments you can verify on‑chain.
